intent: Compare how the shares of adult unauthorized immigrants residing in the U.S. for more than ten years versus five years or less changed between 1995 and 2017.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How did the share of adult unauthorized immigrants residing in the U.S. for more than ten years change between 1995 and 2017?
How did the share of adult unauthorized immigrants residing in the U.S. for five years or less change between 1995 and 2017?
How do the changes in shares for the two duration groups compare between 1995 and 2017?

units.claim: All 2 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The share of adult unauthorized immigrants residing in the U.S. for more than ten years increased from 33% in 1995 to 66% in 2017.
units.computation: Compare first (1995) and last (2017) values for the 'More than 10 years' series: 33% to 66%.
accept: Share for more than 10 years rose from 33% to 66% between 1995 and 2017.
More than 10 years increased by 33 percentage points over the period.
reject: Share for more than 10 years decreased.
Share for more than 10 years remained flat.

units.claim: The share of adult unauthorized immigrants residing in the U.S. for five years or less decreased from 36% in 1995 to 20% in 2017.
units.computation: Compare first (1995) and last (2017) values for the '5 years or less' series: 36% to 20%.
accept: Share for 5 years or less fell from 36% to 20% between 1995 and 2017.
5 years or less decreased by 16 percentage points over the period.
reject: Share for 5 years or less increased.
Share for 5 years or less remained flat.

units.claim: Between 1995 and 2017, the share for more than ten years rose (33% to 66%) while the share for five years or less fell (36% to 20%), reversing their relative positions.
units.computation: Compare endpoint changes: More than 10 years +33 pp (33→66); 5 years or less -16 pp (36→20). In 1995 the 5-years-or-less share was higher (36% vs 33%); by 2017 the more-than-10-years share was much higher (66% vs 20%).
accept: The two groups moved in opposite directions: more than 10 years increased while 5 years or less decreased.
The more-than-10-years share overtook the 5-years-or-less share between 1995 and 2017.
reject: The 5-years-or-less share remained higher than the more-than-10-years share in 2017.

optional_valid: Mentioning intermediate values such as 50% in 2010 for more than 10 years or 23% in 2010 for 5 years or less.
Noting the crossing point occurs between 1995 and 2000 when the more-than-10-years share surpasses the 5-years-or-less share.
unsupported_to_avoid: Claims about absolute numbers of immigrants rather than shares.
Data for years not present in the table (e.g., 2015).
review_notes: The x-axis anchors include 2013 but the 'More than 10 years' series has 2012 instead; each series uses its own listed x-values.
The intent asks for comparison of changes between 1995 and 2017, so endpoint-based trend units and one cross-series comparison unit cover the requested analytical operations.
